evals.prompt: Run a best-practices check on the Argo CD manifests in ./testdata and summarize the issues.
evals.expected_output: Locates or downloads octodoctor, runs it in directory mode against ./testdata, creates testdata/octodoctor-output/{index.html,report.json,report.yaml}, and gives a chat summary of failed/passed/inactive rule counts plus the failed rules ordered by severity with doc links and affected files. Points the user to index.html.
expectations: Ran octodoctor in directory mode (-d/--directory) against ./testdata, not export mode
report.json produced is valid JSON with metadata/summary/results top-level keys matching octodoctor's schema
The failed/passed/inactive rule counts stated in the chat summary match report.json's summary.rules numbers
Chat summary lists at least one failed rule along with its severity
Chat summary tells the user a real, existing path to index.html
Did not ask the user any clarifying questions before running, since the directory and intent were unambiguous

evals.prompt: Can you audit my local Argo CD install for best practices? It's just running on my current cluster.
evals.expected_output: Infers export mode (no directory given), uses whatever kubectl's current context resolves to without asking since it's unambiguous, defaults namespace to argocd, runs octodoctor -e, and summarizes the resulting report. Mentions that secret values are redacted before analysis. Points to the generated index.html.
expectations: Ran octodoctor in export mode (-e/--export), not directory mode
Used whatever kubectl's current context resolves to, without stopping to ask which context to use
Used the argocd namespace (the default) without asking, since the user didn't name a different one
Mentions to the user that secret values are redacted/not exposed during export
report.json produced is valid JSON matching octodoctor's schema
The failed/passed/inactive rule counts stated in the chat summary match report.json's summary.rules numbers
Chat summary tells the user a real, existing path to index.html

evals.prompt: I inherited this Argo CD repo at ./testdata/r19 — can you tell me if it's set up well, following best practices?
evals.expected_output: Triggers the skill despite no mention of 'octodoctor' or any flag. Runs directory mode against ./testdata/r19 and gives a sensible best-practices summary (this fixture directory has a known mix of pass/fail/inactive Application manifests).
expectations: Recognized this as a job for octodoctor even though the user never named the tool or a flag
Ran octodoctor in directory mode against ./testdata/r19 specifically, not the whole testdata tree
report.json produced under testdata/r19/octodoctor-output is valid JSON matching octodoctor's schema
The failed/passed/inactive rule counts stated in the chat summary match report.json's summary.rules numbers
Response is framed as an answer to a plain best-practices question, not just a raw dump of rule IDs
